lessons.title: The five senses

objectives: Name the five senses and the organs for each.
Explain how the senses keep us safe.
Describe simple ways to protect the eyes and the ears.
reviewNotes: Health and nutrition content is kept at a basic, conservative level; to be checked by a teacher or a health worker. The four basic tastes are used (some books add a fifth, umami).

blocks.title: Senses
blocks.md: We have **five senses**. **Sight**: we see with our **eyes**. **Hearing**: we hear with our **ears**. **Smell**: we smell with the **nose**. **Taste**: we taste with the **tongue** (sweet, sour, salty, bitter). **Touch**: we feel with the **skin** (hot, cold, soft, rough, pain). **Nerves** carry messages from the sense organs to the brain.

blocks.caption: The five senses and their organs.
blocks.alt: Five boxes: sight with eyes, hearing with ears, smell with nose, taste with tongue and touch with skin.

blocks.title: Senses keep us safe
blocks.md: The senses warn us of danger: we see a car, hear a horn, smell smoke, taste food that has gone bad and feel a hot pot. The brain tells our muscles to react. People who cannot see or hear use other senses, and tools such as glasses, white canes or hearing aids help them.

blocks.title: Protecting the eyes and ears
blocks.md:
- Never look straight at the sun.
- Read and write with enough light; sit properly.
- Do not put objects (sticks, pins) in your eyes or ears.
- Do not listen to very loud music or stay near very loud noise.
- Tell a teacher or parent if you cannot see the board or hear well.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- Thinking that the tongue only tastes: the **nose** helps us taste (when we have a cold, food has less taste).
- Thinking that touch is only in the hands: the **skin** covers the whole body.
- Tasting an unknown substance to find out what it is: this can be dangerous.

blocks.title: Example 1
blocks.statement: Which sense do we use to know that a pot is hot? Which organ?
steps: That is the sense of touch and the organ is the skin.

blocks.title: Example 2
blocks.statement: You smell smoke at night. Which sense warns you, and what should you do?
steps: Wake others, leave the house calmly and call for help.
blocks.answer: The sense of smell; you should warn others and leave the house at once.

lessons.title: Teeth and a balanced diet
lessons.programRef: MINEDUB primary school curriculum (English-speaking subsystem), Level III — Elementary Science and Technology; to be checked against the official texts

objectives: Name the four kinds of teeth and their jobs.
Explain how to prevent tooth decay.
List the food groups and plan a balanced meal.
reviewNotes: Health and nutrition content is kept at a basic, conservative level; to be checked by a teacher or a health worker. Number of teeth (20 milk, 32 permanent) is the usual textbook figure.
Food examples are local, but nutritional claims are simplified.
Syllabus references, scope and level of difficulty are to be checked against the official text; all facts, formulas and worked examples to be verified by a teacher before release.

blocks.title: Teeth
blocks.md: Children first have **20 milk teeth**. They fall out and are replaced by **permanent teeth**; an adult has up to **32**. There are four kinds: **incisors** (at the front, they cut), **canines** (pointed, they tear), **premolars** and **molars** (at the back, they crush and grind food). A tooth has a hard white **enamel** on the outside.

blocks.caption: The four kinds of teeth and their jobs.
blocks.alt: Four boxes: incisors cut, canines tear, premolars crush and molars grind.

blocks.title: Caring for teeth
blocks.md: Sugar and bits of food left on the teeth feed bacteria, which make an acid that makes holes in the teeth (**tooth decay**). To keep the teeth healthy: brush them **twice a day** (morning and before bed), eat **less sugar** and sweets, drink water, eat fruits and vegetables, and see a **dentist or health worker** when you have toothache.

blocks.title: A balanced diet
blocks.md: A **balanced diet** has food from every group, in the right amounts. **Energy foods** give energy (rice, cassava, plantain, maize, oil). **Body-building foods** (proteins) help us grow and repair the body (beans, fish, eggs, meat, groundnuts). **Protective foods** (vitamins and minerals) keep us healthy (fruits, vegetables). We also need **water** and **fibre** (vegetables, whole grains).

blocks.caption: The food groups.
blocks.alt: Four boxes: energy foods (rice, cassava, plantain), body-building foods (beans, fish, eggs), protective foods (fruits, vegetables) and water and fibre.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- Thinking that only one food group is enough: a child who eats only rice lacks proteins and vitamins.
- Brushing teeth only when they hurt.
- Eating sweets just before bed.
- Thinking that more expensive food is always better: many cheap local foods (beans, groundnuts, vegetables) are very good.

blocks.title: Example 1
blocks.statement: Say which food group each food mostly belongs to: rice, beans, oranges.
steps: Beans help the body to grow: body-building (protein).
blocks.answer: rice: energy; beans: body-building; oranges: protective.

blocks.title: Example 2
blocks.statement: Make a balanced meal from: plantain, fish, eru leaves, a banana, water.
steps: Plantain gives energy; fish gives protein for growth.
Eru leaves and the banana give vitamins; water completes the meal.
blocks.answer: Plantain (energy), fish (body-building), eru and a banana (protective), with water.
